translationRepairs: After Emperor Gaozu captured the capital, he asked He Wuji, "I urgently need a chief clerk for headquarters. How can I find the right man?"
After Emperor Gaozu captured Jingcheng (Jingkou), he asked He Wuji, "I urgently need a chief clerk for headquarters. How can I find the right man?"
京城 here is the walled city of Jingkou (京口城), where Gaozu raised his revolt; the capital (Jiankang) is taken only later (平京邑, s0020). Identification from standard history.
Muzhi had heard shouting and uproar in the capital; rising early he went out to the roadside, where he happened upon the courier.
Muzhi had heard shouting and uproar in Jingcheng (Jingkou); rising early he went out to the roadside, where he happened upon the courier.
京城 is Jingkou city, where Muzhi's family lived (世居京口, s0003), not the capital.

In the third year of Yixi, when Grand Administrator of Yangzhou Wang Mi died, Emperor Gaozu was next in line to enter the capital as chief minister. Liu Yi and others did not want him to do so and proposed making Central Commander of the Army Xie Hun governor of Yangzhou instead.

In the third year of Yixi, when Inspector of Yangzhou Wang Mi died, Emperor Gaozu was next in line to enter the capital as chief minister. Liu Yi and others did not want him to do so and proposed making Central Commander of the Army Xie Hun governor of Yangzhou instead.
刺史 is the regional inspector (governor) of a province, not a grand administrator (太守).
I have received your grace. By right I cannot conceal anything. That is why Zhang Liao reported to Guan Yu that someone wished to rebel."
I have received your grace. By right I cannot conceal anything. That is why Zhang Liao reported that Guan Yu wished to desert."
告關羽欲叛: Zhang Liao reported that Guan Yu intended to desert (叛); Guan Yu is the object of the report, not its recipient.

Of all he recommended for advancement, he did not stop until they were promoted. He often said, "Though I do not match Director Ling of Xun in recommending the worthy, I never recommend the unworthy."
Of all he recommended for advancement, he did not stop until they were promoted. He often said, "Though I do not match Director Xun in recommending the worthy, I never recommend the unworthy."
荀令君 is "Director Xun" (令君 is the honorific for the Director of the Masters of Writing); "Ling" is not a name.
Muzhi was given the additional title General Who Establishes Martial Might, with staff officers appointed and substantive forces allotted to him.
Muzhi was given the additional title General Who Establishes Awe, with staff officers appointed and substantive forces allotted to him.
建威將軍 (jianwei) differs from 建武將軍 (s0005); 威 is awe/might, not "martial".
Muzhi replied, "Your Lordship is campaigning far upstream while entrusting your aged mother and young children to his command. If he failed in the slightest, how could matters stand thus?"
Muzhi replied, "His Lordship is campaigning far upstream while entrusting his aged mother and young children to you. If you failed in the slightest, how could matters stand thus?"
公 here is Gaozu (the Grand Commandant) and 節下 is the addressee Changmin; the translation reverses the referents.
In the eleventh year Emperor Gaozu marched west against Sima Xiuzhi. Central Army General Daolin nominally held the rear post, yet in affairs great and small Muzhi alone decided.
In the eleventh year Emperor Gaozu marched west against Sima Xiuzhi. Central Army General Daolian nominally held the rear post, yet in affairs great and small Muzhi alone decided.
道憐 is read Daolian; 憐 is lian, not lin.

When Muzhi died, the duties of the capital stood vacant. Emperor Gaozu galloped back to Pengcheng and had Secretariat Director Xu Xianzhi take over the rear post, while great affairs of court that Muzhi had regularly decided were all referred north for consultation.

When Muzhi died, the duties of the capital stood vacant. Emperor Gaozu galloped back to Pengcheng and had Major Xu Xianzhi take over the rear post, while great affairs of court that Muzhi had regularly decided were all referred north for consultation.
司馬 here is the office of major (adjutant), not Secretariat Director.

The civil and military staff of Muzhi's Forward Army headquarters numbered twenty thousand. Three thousand were allotted to Xianzhi's Establish Martial Might headquarters, and the rest all to the heir's Central Army headquarters.

The civil and military staff of Muzhi's Forward Army headquarters numbered twenty thousand. Three thousand were allotted to Xianzhi's Establishing Awe headquarters, and the rest all to the heir's Central Army headquarters.
建威府 is the headquarters of the General Who Establishes Awe (建威), not 建武.
Posthumously Muzhi was enfeoffed as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, defender general, and commissioner equal to the three excellencies with an office of his own.
Posthumously Muzhi was granted the titles of regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, defender general, and commissioner equal to the three excellencies with an office of his own.
追贈 confers posthumous offices, not an enfeoffment; the fief comes later (s0121).

The late Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Former General, your servant Muzhi,[5] rose from commoner rank to assist from the very start of our righteous enterprise, setting plans straight within and diligently handling civil affairs without, attending confidentially to military and state matters until mind and strength were both spent.

The late Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Forward General, your servant Muzhi,[5] rose from commoner rank to assist from the very start of our righteous enterprise, setting plans straight within and diligently handling civil affairs without, attending confidentially to military and state matters until mind and strength were both spent.
前將軍 is the Forward General (s0078); "late" already renders 故.
When the Founding Emperor returned, Changmin was executed where he lay prostrate.
When the Founding Emperor returned, Changmin was executed.
伏誅 is an idiom meaning "suffered execution"; 伏 does not mean lying prostrate.
In the ninth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wu, he was allotted sacrificial food in Emperor Gaozu's temple court.
In the ninth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, he was allotted sacrificial food in Emperor Gaozu's temple court.
太祖 in the Book of Song is Emperor Wen (reign title Yuanjia), not Emperor Wu (高祖).
Prince of Hedong Xinzhi had once served as administrator of Nankang and always looked down on Yong.
Wang Xinzhi of Hedong had once served as administrator of Nankang and always looked down on Yong.
河東王歆之 is Wang Xinzhi (surname 王) of Hedong; he was an administrator, not a prince.
After Yong left, Lingxiu wrote to He Xu: "When Liu Yong turned and saw me being devoured, my whole body bled."
After Yong left, Lingxiu wrote to He Xu: "Liu Yong came calling just now and ate from me, so that my whole body ran with blood."
向顧見噉: 向 "just now", 顧 "paid a visit", 見噉 "I was eaten from"; Yong did not "turn and see" anything.
Yan's younger brother Yu, courtesy name Maolin, from youth had talent and spirit, and was known to Emperor Wu.
Yan's younger brother Yu, courtesy name Maolin, from youth had talent and spirit, and was known to Emperor Wen.
太祖 is Emperor Wen of Song, not Emperor Wu.
Jun was greatly angered and memorialized Emperor Wu to transfer Mai to Guangzhou.
Jun was greatly angered and memorialized Emperor Wen to transfer Mai to Guangzhou.
太祖 is Emperor Wen of Song, not Emperor Wu.

Reaching Jiangling, he wrote to Yan Jun: "Zhu Xiuzhi — rebel soldier for three generations — suddenly holds Jing Province. Under the green-oil canopy he receives audiences like Xie Xuanyuan, and had ritual masters with long knives lead me down from my seat.

Reaching Jiangling, he wrote to Yan Jun: "Zhu Xiuzhi — rebel soldier for three generations — suddenly holds Jing Province. Under the green-oil canopy he receives audiences like Xie Xuanming, and had ritual masters with long knives lead me down from my seat.
謝宣明 is read Xie Xuanming (courtesy name of Xie Hui); 明 is ming, not yuan.

When his clansman uncle Xiuzhi became Intendant of Danyang, Yu wrote again to kinsmen and friends: "That dark-faced Little Xi of our house now sits among Liu Anzhong's crowd,[9] as though the court were no assembly of true talent."

When his clansman uncle Xiuzhi became Intendant of Danyang, Yu wrote again to kinsmen and friends: "That dark-faced Little Xiu of our house now sits among Liu Anzhong's crowd,[9] as though the court were no assembly of true talent."
阿秀 is "A Xiu" (Little Xiu), from Xiuzhi's given name; "Xi" is a misreading.
He was posthumously titled Gengzi, "The Forceful."
He was posthumously titled Viscount Gang ("The Forceful").
剛子 = posthumous name 剛 (gang) plus the rank 子 (viscount); it is not a single name "Gengzi".
His son Juan served as Vice Director of Southern Xuzhou.
His son Juan served as Attendant Official (biejia) of South Xuzhou.
別駕 is the provincial attendant official (biejia), not a vice director.

The bureau in direct charge must know the work thoroughly; moreover, Na, staff officer of the Eastern Bureau's Board of Works and Water Board, recently assigned this duty, is quite capable and would suffice on his own.

The bureau in direct charge must know the work thoroughly; moreover, Nazhi, staff officer of the Eastern Bureau's Board of Works and Water Board, recently assigned this duty, is quite capable and would suffice on his own.
納之 is a two-character given name (Nazhi); the translation drops 之.

Before his mourning was complete, Rear General Sima Yuansian wished to appoint him Adviser with the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distant and charge of secretarial affairs; Hong firmly declined.

Before his mourning was complete, Rear General Sima Yuanxian wished to appoint him Adviser with the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distant and charge of secretarial affairs; Hong firmly declined.
司馬元顯 is Sima Yuanxian; "Yuansian" is a misspelling.
He submitted a memorial firmly declining: "I have heard that Duke Wu of Zhao praised Suí Huì's household as well governed, saying that to the state of Jin there was no concealment.
He submitted a memorial firmly declining: "I have heard that Zhao Wu praised Sui Hui's household as well governed, saying that to the state of Jin there was no concealment.
趙武 is the personal name of the Jin minister Zhao Wu, not a "Duke Wu of Zhao"; 隨會 is Sui Hui (diacritics inconsistent with the rest of the text).
Liu Muzhi was then in charge at the capital, but the emperor's intent arrived from the north; stricken with shame and fear, Muzhi fell ill and died.
Liu Muzhi was then in charge at the capital, but the instruction came directly from the north; stricken with shame and fear, Muzhi fell ill and died.
旨 here is Gaozu's instruction (he was not yet emperor); the point is that it bypassed Muzhi in the capital.

He was further granted the insignia of envoy and made Palace Attendant; his post as inspector was changed to military commissioner; his title was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry; his grand headquarters and provincial post remained as before.

He was further granted the insignia of envoy and made Palace Attendant; his post as supervisor of military affairs was changed to commander-in-chief; his title was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry; his grand headquarters and provincial post remained as before.
改監為都督: his supervisorship (監, s0539) was upgraded to commander-in-chief (都督); his inspectorship (刺史) remained "as before".
Thus the Elder Lord of Teng in Lu was praised in the Spring and Autumn Annals, while Chu sent Qi Ji into exile — the earlier histories preserve both the model and the warning.

Thus Lu's giving precedence to the Lord of Teng was praised in the Spring and Autumn Annals, while Chu's sending Qiji out of the capital — the earlier histories preserve both the model and the warning.
魯長滕君: Lu ranked the Lord of Teng first (長 is a verb); there is no "Elder Lord". 楚出棄疾: Chu sent Prince Qiji out to govern, not into exile.
My lord stands at the pinnacle of government, the whole realm looks to you, toiling from dawn to dusk with a devotion equal to Duke Zhou's "spitting in his palm and clasping hands."

My lord stands at the pinnacle of government, the whole realm looks to you, toiling from dawn to dusk with a devotion equal to the Duke of Zhou, who "spat out his food and clutched his hair" to receive worthy men.
吐握 alludes to the Duke of Zhou spitting out his food and clutching his half-washed hair to receive visitors, not spitting in his palm.

In a letter to the heads of the chief ministries and their department directors, he wrote: "When members of the same household register violate the law, there is no statute that punishes men of the gentry class directly, yet whenever punishment is imposed, appeals are always lodged.

In a letter to the heads of the chief ministries and their department directors, he wrote: "When members of the same household register violate the law, there is no statute exempting men of the gentry class from punishment, yet whenever punishment is imposed, appeals are always lodged.
無士人不罪之科 means there is no rule that gentry are not punished; the translation inverted it.

[16] He also noted that stealing five bolts was punishable by death for a chief storekeeper and forty bolts for an ordinary keeper — punishments all agreed were too severe. He proposed raising the threshold to ten bolts for a chief keeper and fifty for an ordinary keeper before imposing death, with theft of forty bolts reduced to conscription as a soldier.

[16] He also noted that theft of five bolts by a storekeeper in charge and of forty bolts in ordinary theft were both punishable by death — punishments all agreed were too severe. He proposed raising the threshold to ten bolts for a storekeeper in charge and fifty bolts for ordinary theft before imposing death, with theft of forty bolts reduced to conscription as a soldier.
常偷 is ordinary theft (as 常盜 in s0401), not theft by an "ordinary keeper".
If members of the same register were again treated alike and relegated to military service along with common offenders, I believe that would be unduly harsh.
If they were further lumped together with common offenders and relegated to military service, I believe that would be unduly harsh.
雷同羣小 means lumping the gentry together with the petty crowd; the subject is the convicted gentry, not register members.

The Left Assistant Director argued that bond-servants and retainers are connected to neighboring ward registers and can therefore be supervised; when an offense appears on the register, their masters should bear criminal liability.

The Left Assistant Director argued that bond-servants and retainers are connected to neighboring ward registers and can therefore be supervised; when an offense appears on the register, the bond-servants and retainers themselves should bear criminal liability.
使及刑坐 refers to the slaves and retainers (cf. s0392-s0393, where the retainer, not the master, is punished).
Having slaves does not make a man unworthy, and lacking slaves does not necessarily make him virtuous.
Having slaves does not make a man worthy, and lacking slaves does not necessarily make him unworthy.
有奴不賢，無奴不必不賢: the polarity was reversed; the point (cf. s0440) is that the slaveless are not less worthy.
During the jiwei reign period, gentry in Kuaiji reported that more than ten years earlier four clans had been punished on the same grounds, but execution was stayed by imperial grace.
Around the jiwei year, gentry in Kuaiji reported that more than ten years earlier four clans had been punished on the same grounds, but execution was stayed by imperial grace.
己未 is a sexagenary year (outside-knowledge conversion: AD 419), not a reign period.

The late General of the Cadet Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Grand Master of the Bright, and Crown Prince's Chamberlain — Marquis Wen of Yunin, Tan Shou —[29] who from youth cherished simplicity and whose conduct was upright and principled.

The late Cadet Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary, Left Grand Master of the Bright, and Crown Prince's Chamberlain — Marquis Wen of Yuning, Tan Shou —[29] who from youth cherished simplicity and whose conduct was upright and principled.
散騎常侍 is not a generalship; 豫寧 is Yuning, not "Yunin".
In youth he once played liubo at Ziye's lodge at Gongcheng; later when he held power, someone came to Hong seeking a county post and pleaded his case quite urgently.
In youth he once played liubo at the country lodge of Gongcheng Ziye; later when he held power, someone came to Hong seeking a county post and pleaded his case quite urgently.
公城子野 reads as a personal name (cf. s0510, where the petitioner asks where he is); 野舍 is a country lodge.
